messages:
lee: Quick sync — planning to run the accounts schema migration tonight in the 01:00-03:00 UTC swing window. Need an owner for deploy, smoke, and rollback readiness. Can @sam or @maya pick this up? Migration includes dual-write for accounts->accounts_v2 and an incremental backfill. Estimated risk: small write fence if we need an emergency rollback, otherwise live during dual-write.
sam: I can own deploy + smoke. Free in that window. Will run through checklist and post timeline.
maya: I can be rollback lead and verify backfill resume. Ping me 10m before cut.
tony: I'll run the staging canary and smoke reads. Preflight command I used: ```bash
./scripts/migration_preflight.sh --env=staging --schema=accounts_v2
```
sre-oncall: I'll monitor the usual metrics (p99 latency, db_error_rate, replication_lag). Please tag me when you start and if the canary shows anomalies.
deploy-bot: deployment request queued by @sam for 01:10 UTC. CID: deploy-1755004321-acc. Plan: canary-proddup -> 10% traffic -> 50% -> full.
maya: Rollback plan quick note: 1) stop dual-write, 2) switch writes back to accounts, 3) run rollback function: ```psql -c "SELECT rollback_accounts_v2();"```, 4) verify consistency with sample queries. Estimated recovery time 30-60m depending on backfill state.
lee: Owner map: deploy=@sam, rollback=@maya, preflight=@tony, oncall=@sre-oncall. @sam confirm exact start time and post runbook link here.
sam: Confirmed. Canary start 01:10 UTC on prod-dup, start dual-write 01:20, kick backfill 01:30. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/migrations/accounts_v2. I'll post smoke logs and short diffs.
maya: I'll run a dry rollback against prod-dup after canary (~01:18) and report status here.
tony: Staging preflight showed: OK — schema apply, feature flag enabled, no obvious FK issues. Snippet: `OK: migrations apply, kv-cache warm`.
lee: Perfect. If we hit >0.5% write errors or replication lag >5s we abort to rollback plan. :thumbsup: 
sam: noted. Will post live timestamps and attach `deploy` output. If anything unexpected, call paging list and we'll follow the rollback steps.
